title: Dniprorudne
summary: Dniprorudne is a city located in the Vasylivka Raion of Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, with a population of 17,736 as of 2022. It has been recognized as a city since 1970 and has played a significant role during the ongoing conflict [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

sections.heading: Geographical and Administrative Context
paragraphs: Dniprorudne is situated in the [[vasylivka|Vasylivka]] Raion within the [[zaporizhzhia-oblast|Zaporizhzhia Oblast]] of [[ukraine|Ukraine]].

sections.heading: History
paragraphs: Dniprorudne has held city status since 1970.
In the early stages of the [[2022-russian-invasion-of-ukraine|2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], the city was captured by Russian forces.

On 13 March 2022, the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]] reported the abduction of Dniprorudne's mayor, Yevhen Matvieyev, by the Russian military. Matvieyev had been actively protesting against the Russian occupation, including a demonstration on 27 February aimed at preventing Russian tanks from entering the city.
On 4 December 2024, the Ukrainian government announced that Matvieyev had died in Russian captivity under torture, and his body was subsequently returned to Ukraine.

sections.heading: Demographics
paragraphs: As of January 1989, Dniprorudne had a population of 22,773.

By 2001, the population had decreased to 21,271. The demographic composition is predominantly [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]], with Russians representing the largest minority. The city exhibits a nearly equal distribution of Ukrainian and Russian speakers.

sections.heading: Transport
paragraphs: Dniprorudne features an inland port, contributing to its logistical and transport capabilities.
